tieu_de: Uranus transit through the 4th house: shaking up home and roots
mo: Does Uranus in the 4th house mean I will have to move?
Why am I thinking so much about my childhood?
How can I stay grounded when home keeps changing?

Boxes in the hallway, a builder who arrives a week early, a grown child announcing they have found their own flat. When Uranus moves through the 4th house, the most private part of your life stops standing still.

Home is supposed to be the place where nothing surprises you, which is exactly why this transit can feel so unsettling. It is also why it can be so freeing. Old family patterns that sat quietly in the background finally come up for review.

doan: The 4th house describes where you live, the people you live with, your family of origin and the emotional foundations you built your life on. Uranus brings sudden change and a hunger for independence, so in this house it tends to rearrange both the physical home and the inner one.

On the surface that can mean moving, renovating or seeing the household shrink or grow. Deeper down, it is a chance to step out from under the influence of the past: a parent's expectations, a family role you were assigned, or a picture of "home" that belonged to someone else.
Planet Uranus Rules Aquarius Innovation, freedom, surprise
A move that happens faster than planned, or several moves in a short span.
Repairs or renovations that start small and grow into a full redesign.
Children leaving home, relatives moving in, or a change in who holds the keys.
A sudden wish to live somewhere very different: a new city, a smaller place, a shared house, a van.
Memories and family stories surfacing, sometimes with new information attached.
Wanting more say over your own space, even inside a shared household.

This transit lets you build a home that fits who you are now. If you have been living in a place chosen for a past version of yourself, you can finally change it. People often end the transit with a living space that feels unusually personal, whether that is a minimalist flat or a noisy house full of projects.
The emotional side can be just as valuable. Uranus loosens the grip of old family rules, and many people find they can see their parents more clearly and relate to them with less guilt.

Instability at home can leave you feeling as if the floor is moving. Sleep, routine and the sense of having somewhere safe to land can all be disrupted, especially during a move or major works. Family members may resist the changes you want, or make changes of their own that you did not agree to.
There is also a risk of cutting ties too sharply. Wanting independence from the past does not require burning every bridge to it.

Uranus spends about 7 years in each sign, so a 4th house transit usually unfolds over several years. The exact length depends on the size of your 4th house, which changes with the house system and your latitude at birth. If Uranus crosses the IC, the cusp of this house, the first stretch is often the most eventful.
Keep a portable "home base" that does not depend on the house: a routine, a ritual, a corner that stays the same.
Budget renovations with a large buffer. Uranus projects tend to expand.
Before moving, list what the new place must give you that the old one cannot.
Talk with family about changes before they happen, not after.
Use this time to look honestly at inherited habits. Keep the ones that help and drop the ones that only repeat.

Many people do move during this transit, but not all. Some renovate, some change who they live with, and some change how they feel about the same address. The common thread is that home stops being fixed.
The 4th house holds your roots, and Uranus brings buried material up suddenly. Old memories often return so you can see them with adult eyes and decide what still has a hold on you.
Anchor yourself in routines rather than places. Regular meals, sleep times and one or two familiar objects can give you stability while the bigger picture reorganises.
